To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the impact of mental disorders on work loss is similar to that of chronic physical disorders; (2) mental disorders are associated with more presenteeism than absenteeism; and (3) at population-level, major depressive disorder, chronic back pain and respiratory disorders contribute the most to total work loss.
mental disorders are associated with more work loss days than physical disorders, and that the costs of these losses are substantial.
Any mental or physical disorder is associated with additional work loss days.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic consequences of mental and physical health conditions on the workforce in the Netherlands.
the impact of mental disorders on productivity.
the effects of mental disorders on work performance, and the associated costs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mental disorders have a greater impact on work loss than physical disorders, but that the total impact of physical disorders is greater than the impact of mental disorders, because physical disorders are more prevalent.
the effects on work loss of mental disorders are at least as large as those of physical disorders.
both physical and mental disorders are associated with a considerable number of days of absenteeism and presentism and that the costs associated with these disorders are considerable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mental health is as important for productivity as physical health.
the effects of both mental and physical disorders on work performance should be taken into account when estimating the burden of diseases and when planning preventive and curative interventions.

the impact of mental disorders on work performance is comparable to the impact of physical disorders, and that both types of disorders contribute substantially to total annual work loss days in the Netherlands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both mental and physical disorders contribute to work loss and that mental disorders are not less costly than physical ones.
the costs of (mental and physical) disorders to employers are substantial.
the burden of (mental) health disorders on workers is substantial.
